headline: Treasury Official Renews Warning on Wave of Tax-Saving Trades
author: Justina Lee

paragraphs.text: Thu, November 19, 2026 at 2:31 PM PST 2 min read

(Bloomberg) -- A senior US Treasury official reiterated concerns Thursday about Wall Street's tax-efficient investing boom, saying firms should win clients on the merits of their investments, not on how far they'll go to minimize a tax bill.

Kevin Salinger, acting assistant secretary for tax policy at the Treasury, spoke at a Wall Street Tax Association conference in New York. His comments come after the department in late September issued a ruling on a strategy that uses exchange-traded funds to avoid capital gains taxes, along with a notice warning of possible action on other tactics.

"Businesses should be competing on investment performance, on fees, and on service," said Salinger, who is also acting chief counsel for the Internal Revenue Service. "Businesses should not be competing on who can take most tax risk and expose their investors to the most tax risk."

Salinger offered few new details on what action might be in store following the September notice, which identified tactics ranging from hedge funds that cut income tax to exchange-traded funds that turn interest income into capital gains. The rhetoric from government has been steadily increasing, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent saying last week that eliminating what he called "tax gimmicks" could help reduce the US budget deficit, without raising tax rates.

The recent IRS notice is "not necessarily exhaustive" and the government continues to "learn about new transactions that taxpayers are engaging in," Salinger added, without naming any additional trades. He reiterated the government has a range of tools at its disposal, including guidance and enforcement actions.

The business of tax-aware investing has proved highly lucrative for Wall Street, as it lures assets and earns fees from the growing ranks of wealthy Americans. Most are in products that harvest capital losses to offset gains from selling investments like a private business or equity holding, but a small group of firms has even found ways to generate ordinary losses that can offset income such as wages.

AQR Capital Management, the quant investing giant co-founded by Cliff Asness, has been at the forefront of the industry. A spokesperson for the firm didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
